forces: A previously shipped, tested single-attempt handoff must gain a caller-supplied attempt ordinal without breaking any existing caller or loosening its fail-closed outcome classification.
Retry scheduling needs full determinism under test — bounded delay, jitter, and timing — without the module itself reading wall-clock time or an unseeded random source.

The retry budget and wire correlation must respect the frozen contract's retry_attempt_max ceiling and the delivery conformance contract's attempt-identity requirement without the module reading the frozen contract source or requiring a contract change.
Retry scheduling must stay compositional and separate from the single-attempt handoff's own scope, preserving the existing requirement that the handoff module itself never schedules a retry.

approach-alternative-implement-delivery-.reason: Folding scheduling into the handoff module would directly contradict the shipped requirement that the single-attempt handoff never itself schedules a retry, would force every existing handoff test to carry fake-timer setup it does not need, and would couple HTTP outcome classification to backoff/jitter concerns that #105 and #106 will also need to compose against independently.

evidence_ids: wire-correlation test asserts the supplied ordinal reaches correlation.retry_attempt and the result without mutating event.id
out-of-bounds ordinal test asserts a negative, non-integer, or over-ceiling ordinal is rejected before any exchange call
only-retries-retryable test: a non_retryable/acknowledged/protocol_error outcome stops scheduling immediately
outcome-mutation test: a retryable outcome followed by a permanent outcome makes exactly two attempts, never three
max-attempts test: an always-retryable handoff produces exactly maxAttempts calls and a terminal exhausted result with an attempt counter
single-attempt boundary test: maxAttempts=1 makes exactly one call and schedules no delay
construction-validation test: out-of-range maxAttempts, negative delays, and maxDelayMs < baseDelayMs all throw TypeError before any attempt
delay-computation test: exact expected delays asserted for a fixed jitter source and base/max delay configuration
delay-cap test: an uncapped exponential value is clamped to maxDelayMs
jitter-range test: a jitter source returning a value outside [0, 1) is rejected
